rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hypocritical group attends the Prophet without seeking understanding, then asks the gathering's knowledgeable people what he said after they leave.
rows.anchor: when these people disperse from his presence, they ask from other knowledgeable people of the gathering what the Prophet (sws) had said

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among those who reject revelation, one group avoids the Prophet out of aversion, while another comes only to feign listening; both are hypocritical.
rows.anchor: another one among them comes to him but not to listen and to understand; only to display its hypocrisy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question about what he said lets them pretend they heard him and are ready to obey, while claiming they could not understand, thus concealing hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: as far as hearing the Prophet (sws) is concerned, they have fully heard what he has said

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They insinuate that revelation needs deep deliberation and that believers accept the Prophet's words as simpletons; this tactic undermines the message, as their taunt about whose faith a sūrah revived illustrates.
rows.anchor: by this comment they would insinuate agony for the Muslims who would believe and show conviction in everything related to them by the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A revealed sūrah increases believers in faith and joy, while adding impurity to the hypocrites until they die in disbelief.
rows.anchor: It will surely increase the believers’ faith and give them joy. As for those whose hearts are tainted, it will add uncleanness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described in verse 16 are like the people in verse 14: their misdeeds have become attractive, so they follow base desires and face the same fate.
rows.anchor: their misdeeds have been endeared to them and they have become the followers of their base desires

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By their misdeeds, such people lose the innate light of vision and therefore remain deprived of revelation and have sealed hearts.
rows.anchor: Such people deprive themselves of the light of vision which the Almighty has innately blessed man with

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases the guidance of those who preserve their innate light and nurtures their virtue according to their capacity and desire; hypocrites lose even their innate ability.
rows.anchor: God, through His companionship of His Prophet (sws), increased such people in guidance as had kept intact the innate light

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to understand the Prophet means they are waiting for the Hour to overtake them; the Hour can mean the Last Day or the decisive punishment of a messenger's rejecters, with one prefiguring the other.
rows.anchor: The word “hour” can refer to both the Day of Judgement and as well as to the decisive punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a messenger and revealed a book so the people have no excuse; they only pretend ignorance, and if they refuse reminders, they are effectively asking for punishment and the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: God sends His messenger to convey the truth to the extent that no one is left with an excuse to deny it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour's signs have appeared: God's established practice is to send decisive punishment only after a messenger reaches a people's central city; this has happened, and respite still gives them a chance to reform despite deserving punishment.
rows.anchor: the Almighty does not send His decisive punishment to a people unless He sends His messenger to their central city

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people still ignore the signs, God will separate the pious and destroy the persistently rebellious; worldly signs will grow clearer, and a worldly court of justice after the final Messenger will prefigure the greater Hereafter judgment.
rows.anchor: God will separate His pious people and will destroy those adamant on rebelliousness and anarchy

rows.speaker: Prophet (sws)
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly raised two adjacent fingers to show that his advent and the Day of Judgment are close to each other.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) has referred to this by raising his two fingers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the subject of the verb “came” in the sentence is the previously mentioned Hour.
rows.anchor: the subject of the verb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they wait to believe until the Hour arrives, whether as punishment or the Last Day, it will be too late: reminders benefit only before it comes.
rows.anchor: once it arrives, their professing faith will be absolutely useless

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As judgment nears, people should recognize that God alone is deity; those relying on alleged deities will realize no one can protect them from God.
rows.anchor: People who have no fear of God on the basis of their alleged deities will come to fully realize by that time that no one is there to help them against God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to seek forgiveness for himself and the believers as preparation for that day's calamities, leaving those heedless of them to themselves.
rows.anchor: he should keep asking the forgiveness of God for his blemishes and for that of the believers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address casts the Prophet as his community's representative and intercessor, bearing its burden and diligently seeking forgiveness for both men and women among the believers.
rows.anchor: This address to the Prophet (sws) is in his capacity of the representative and intercessor of his people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's blemishes are attributed to him as representative of the community, not directly; they arise from zeal for truth rather than base desire and are corrected because prophets exemplify truth and falsehood.
rows.anchor: the blemishes of the prophets of God do not emanate from base desires; their blemishes emanate from being over zealous for the cause of truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word mutaqallabakum can be a verbal noun or an adverb of place; the author chooses the place sense because it contrasts with mathwā, a place of residence.
rows.anchor: I have interpreted it in the latter sense because it is used in contrast with

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness assures the Prophet and Muslims of protection wherever they go or reside, since God knows their frequented places and homes.
rows.anchor: He will protect them wherever they are; He knows full well the places they frequent and as well as their abodes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 20 recalls the clear jihad directive in verse 4: hypocrites who had bluffed faith and demanded a command recoil when a sūrah makes jihad explicit.
rows.anchor: when they heard the clear directive of jīhad as mentioned in verse four of this sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the explicit jihad sūrah arrived, hypocrites afflicted by envy and hypocrisy stared at the Prophet as if stricken by death's stupor.
rows.anchor: those in whose hearts is the ailment of jealousy and hypocrisy look towards the Prophet (sws) as if they are facing the stupor of death

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An incomplete verb is understood before the quoted words; the implied verb means “they used to say.”
rows.anchor: There is an incomplete verb suppressed before O as per linguistic principles. Keeping this aspect in view, the translation of this verb would be: “they used to say.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who professed faith” describes people claiming the faith expressed by the verb; this is common Arabic usage, as in 4:136.
rows.anchor: this usage is very common in Arabic

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted phrase after “why not a sūrah” is “about jihad” or “about fighting”; Qur'anic style introduces a matter concisely before detailing it, including in 47:36 and the question in 2:189.
rows.anchor: The implied meaning is that first these people fervently demanded that why is not a clear directive regarding jihād revealed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word sūrah can mean either a Qur'anic chapter or a directive, and both senses may apply here.
rows.anchor: has been used in the Qur’ ān for a sūrah of the Qur’ān as well as a directive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective muḥkama signals certainty and such clarity that the directive needs no explanation, is not vague, and is not an ambiguous matter whose reality only God knows.
rows.anchor: shows its certainty and such clarity that requires no explanation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marad here means hypocrisy as well as malice and envy toward Islam and the Prophet, explained again in verses 29 and 37.
rows.anchor: refers to hypocrisy as well as the malice and envy these hypocrites had for Islam and the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A similar hypocritical fear of fighting appears in 4:77: after being told to disarm, pray, and pay zakāh, some fear people as they fear God or more.
rows.anchor: When they were ordered to fight, some of them feared people as
